principles: Confidence must never be manufactured from incomplete identity.
Metadata-only progress should not create repeated expensive work.
One shared lineage primitive should govern trusted metadata descendants.
Observability must distinguish execution from reuse and explain every refusal.
drivers: Preserve fail-closed safety across all validation sources and modes.
Avoid new metadata churn and self-invalidating cache behavior.
Keep DONE-specific proof semantics separate from routine validation.

options.name: A: Shared lineage plus routine validation identity
pros: Reuses existing DONE lineage semantics without copying DONE-only proof rules
cons: Requires evidence schema extension and migration-by-execution

options.name: B: Reuse on materialHash and storyFilesHash only
pros: Would eliminate the observed B-c163 duplicates
cons: Unsound when commands, config, entrypoint, focus/profile, or policy change

options.name: C: Separate cache artifact keyed by HEAD
cons: Misses metadata-descendant cases that caused the waste
Adds another lifecycle artifact and writer
Cache writes can create more HEAD drift

chosen: A: Shared lineage plus routine validation identity
rationale: Option A is the only design that removes the measured waste while retaining fail-closed correctness. It recognizes trusted metadata-only HEAD movement, but requires exact equality of all material, story-file, command, source, entrypoint, mode and verification-policy inputs. It also avoids a second cache artifact and keeps DONE-only build proof outside routine validate.

preMortem.scenario: A changed command or validate config incorrectly reuses an old PASS.
preMortem.trigger: Identity omits normalized command args, cwd, shell, timeout, source or config digest.
preMortem.consequence: Validation reports PASS without executing the changed plan.
preMortem.mitigation: Canonicalize and hash the full resolved plan/source envelope; add one-dimension-at-a-time mismatch tests.

preMortem.scenario: Metadata-only validation commits cause an infinite reuse/write/drift loop.
preMortem.trigger: The reused path rewrites test-evidence or auto-commits a new disposition artifact.
preMortem.consequence: Every reuse moves HEAD and repeatedly invalidates lineage or evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Return reused disposition without writing evidence; assert byte-identical artifact and unchanged HEAD in tests.

preMortem.scenario: HEAD changes between reuse check and return.
preMortem.trigger: Concurrent metadata or source write occurs after the first hash read.
preMortem.consequence: A PASS for one tree is returned for another tree.
preMortem.mitigation: Perform the decision under validation execution lock, read HEAD before and after, and execute on any drift.

preMortem.scenario: Focused or fallback validation is mistaken for full configured validation.
preMortem.trigger: Identity omits focus/full/profile or source/entrypoint digest.
preMortem.consequence: A narrower PASS satisfies a broader validation request.
preMortem.mitigation: Bind mode and source-specific identity fields; add cross-mode and cross-source refusal tests.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy or malformed evidence crashes validation or reuses accidentally.
preMortem.trigger: New fields are assumed present or parser defaults them permissively.
preMortem.mitigation: Treat missing/malformed identity as a named refusal and execute the real plan.
